claims.statement: Talon's `BackgroundSubagents` detaches local `task` and remote `start_async_task` calls for ordinary conversational turns into owner-scoped in-memory jobs, blocks nested delegation and approvals in workers, enforces job and concurrency limits, and exposes only a bounded text result to the owning conversation.

Talon runs subagent delegation inline during scheduled turns because no later conversational turn can consume a detached result; inline calls leave no job, serializes failure or timeout as sanitized error output, queues fan-out beyond the inline concurrency ceiling, and keeps recursion blocked.

`create_deep_agent` routes declarative and compiled synchronous subagents to `SubAgentMiddleware`'s `task` tool, routes `AsyncSubAgent` specifications to `AsyncSubAgentMiddleware`, and can add a default synchronous `general-purpose` child when permitted by the harness profile.

SDK local `task` calls require a tool-call ID and return a correlated result; isolated children receive a task message plus only non-excluded public state, while a declarative fork reconstructs effective parent history and inherits its prompt-producing context whereas a compiled fork excludes private state, and forked calls refuse nested delegation.

An SDK `AsyncSubAgent` is remote Agent Protocol work: its middleware returns task IDs, persists task records in `async_tasks`, and asynchronously observes unfinished tasks to inject changed outcomes into the parent.

Declarative SDK children inherit parent filesystem permissions and `interrupt_on` unless they override those fields, whereas compiled runnables and remote async subagents do not inherit the top-level interrupt configuration.

When an explicit filesystem-tool allowlist is active, dcode injects restricted `FilesystemMiddleware` into synchronous declarative children and rejects compiled children because their middleware cannot be safely injected; remote async children use their own backend.

Talon rejects fork mode and compiles local roles as fresh task-only graphs with explicitly attached tools and Talon approval/control middleware; it refuses an opaque compiled child when approval policy must be enforced inside it.
`SkillsMiddleware` caches a source-ordered, last-one-wins skill index in state; it exposes skill metadata first and can pin readable skill bodies before the next model call.

A successful read or pin of a skill with `metadata.include_tools` can disclose its deferred or middleware-owned tools for the next model call, anchored at the first qualifying read; the middleware records only tools actually disclosed and admits an otherwise-unregistered call only through that latest recorded include-name path.
Dcode orders built-in, plugin, user, project, and experimental Claude skill sources from lower to higher precedence, and logs plugin-discovery failure while continuing to add local sources.

`SubAgentMiddleware` serializes a structured child response as JSON or otherwise its last non-empty AI text, and converts recognized returned or raised model and structured-output refusals into an explanatory correlated task result rather than raising that refusal through the parent task call.

For a checkpointing SDK local child, `task` places the child run's `checkpoint_ns` in the correlated `ToolMessage.artifact`; compiled graphs are streamed to identify the namespace that saved, nested calls retain namespace ancestry, and no artifact is produced when no child checkpoint was saved. A `.with_retry()` wrapper is a documented limitation because it must be invoked and can report the fallback namespace rather than the successful suffixed retry namespace.

An `AsyncSubAgent` can use experimental fork mode to launch a remote task with a snapshot of effective parent messages plus the delegated description, while isolated mode sends only that description; copying conversation does not make the remote graph inherit parent configuration, and a URL-less ASGI target can be launched only through an async parent entrypoint.

Talon exposes owner-scoped job controls: listings suppress unchanged polls and repeated listed results, inspection returns only bounded metadata/activity and receipts, and messaging is a bounded cooperative inbox available only to Talon-built local workers that is consumed before their next model request.

`DeepAgentRuntime` constructs `BackgroundSubagents` with a positive `DEEPAGENTS_TALON_MAX_BACKGROUND_TASKS` worker limit and an optional `DEEPAGENTS_TALON_INLINE_SUBAGENT_TIMEOUT`, while the middleware keeps detached workers and scheduled inline calls under separate concurrency and timeout policies.

Tool disclosure uses provider-native inline blocks at the stable post-read conversation anchor when the model profile supports mid-conversation tools, preserving the cached prefix; otherwise disclosed tools are bound into the request tool list, and provider-rejected schemas are withheld from both the model and the dispatch record.

Talon keeps conversational background completion separate from delivery: only the owner sees pending results, results are acknowledged after a successful main turn, discarded replies can requeue consumed IDs, and repeated failed deliveries are dropped after three attempts.

Talon's delegation and fresh-worker contracts treat capability inventories and delegated findings as untrusted evidence, require research workers to report unavailable capabilities rather than inventing access, and preserve approval controls; explicit tool attachments can deliberately grant a fresh role a capability but do not make its findings or claimed approvals authoritative.

`SUBAGENT_RESPONSE_FORMAT_CONFIG_KEY` supplies a per-task dynamic response format only for declarative subagents, overriding their static `response_format`; a compiled runnable rejects that override. A fork does not inherit its parent's response format, and differing child formats change provider tool or output configuration, reducing request equivalence needed for potential prompt-cache reuse.
